answer: A trust-graph flow protocol resists Sybil attacks by bounding admission through network cut capacities from seed nodes. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of establishing authentic bilateral peering edges with honest peers per identity. Capping path flow at a structural zenith prevents forged clusters from eclipsing a lone sparrow agent exchanging services like a benchmark sonnet. A key limitation is that honest nodes can be tricked into extending trust edges to adversarial agents.
